newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Friday with investors pessimistic about the short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 22,910 yuan ($2,761) per tonne, unchanged from Thursday's close. It opened at 22,860 and hit a low of 22,840 yuan.
April fell 20 yuan to 23,130, May rose 50 to 23,050, June dropped 10 to 22,960, August 20 to 22,890 and September 30 to 22,870 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 25,910 tonnes from 32,890 tonnes.
Though physical copper prices are higher than futures prices, traders saw near-term falls with the looming end of the high production season.
Aluminium ended mixed. April rose 50 to 15,500 yuan per tonne, May was unchanged at 15,600 and June fell 50 to 15,750.
Combined volume rose to 780 tonnes from 410 tonnes.
Copper opened mostly lower and moved at those levels for most of the session.
Most investors preferred to build short positions at current levels because they do not think copper will rise in the near future on weak market sentiment, traders said.

"Technical charts also indicated possibility for further falls in the short term," one trader said. "Thin trading volume showed many investors taking a wary attitude, especially ahead of the weekend."
Spot copper prices were around 23,400/500 yuan per tonne.
